Arsenal’s fifth draw from five home games in the Women’s Super League left them frustrated once again but this was a wholly different story to the previous four, as they played out an entertaining 1-1 draw with a London City Lionesses side inspired by their goalkeeper Mary Earps.
Aston Villa, Birmingham, Manchester United and Crystal Palace all came to this stadium for a point, defending resolutely and exposing Arsenal’s inability to break down low blocks, whereas London City came to play and were rewarded with a draw that maintains their six‑point advantage over Arsenal in the race for a European place, and moving within six points of the leaders Chelsea.
Earps, producing her best performance to date for the team she joined in the summer, repeatedly denied Frida Maanum and Lisa Baum and was named player of the match in a contest where both goals were scored inside the space of 99 seconds. The impressive Maanum finished off a superb team move for Arsenal to open the scoring in the 10th minute but her goal was cancelled out by a terrific finish from Isobel Goodwin whose head coach, Eder Maestre, said: “We came here to take risks. We really wanted to win.
“Our identity is playing with bravery – we were brave today. We weren’t scared about the context, the opponent, the stadium, nothing. We tried to play as we play at home.”
Arsenal had secured an impressive result in Barcelona on Thursday, drawing with the European champions , but this game against the WSL’s third-placed side felt as though it was of even greater importance, particularly if Arsenal wish to continue visiting venues such as the Camp Nou next season, and they were unable to find a way past Earps to win and close the gap in the table.
Just like they had done away at Anfield last Sunday , Renée Slegers’s team made a bright start with energy, pace and the threat of Alessia Russo. Emily Fox’s shot was deflected wide, after a good move that included some excellent Maanum buildup play, before Ona Batlle’s long-range effort bounced wide. It was not long before Maanum tucked in the opening goal after an intelligent cutback from Russo.
The visitors struck back almost immediately, though, as Goodwin did superbly to turn inside Leah Williamson and then demonstrated strength and composure to hold off Baum and fire a lethal finish past Misa Rodríguez with power and precision. It was a timely moment of class from the English striker in front of the England head coach, Sarina Wiegman, who was in the stands before naming her next England squad on Tuesday morning.
Earps then twice saved from Baum from range. After the break, Earps did well again to dive low to her left to divert a Caitlin Foord strike wide, and what followed was a sustained spell of London City possession, territory and chances. Maestre’s team spent a good part of 20 minutes firmly camped in Arsenal’s half and they carved open a good chance for Kadidiatou Diani but her relatively tame, low, near-post effort was saved by Rodríguez.
Diani’s 62nd-minute replacement from the substitutes’ bench, Delphine Cascarino, drew gasps from the crowd as she unleashed a dipping strike that bounced off the top of the crossbar. It was a lucky escape for Arsenal, who had won all seven of their previous meetings with London City across all competitions but were denied by two more fine Earps stops, firstly from a Maanum close-range effort and then from Maanum’s curler, which looked destined for the top corner before Earps touched it on to the bar.
Viviane Asseyi scored twice as West Ham secured back-to-back WSL home wins after beating rock-bottom Charlton 2-0.
Asseyi’s curled finish put the Irons in front just ahead of the break and she then scored a 25-yard free-kick early in the second half. The defeat saw Charlton, who remain without a point, become the first WSL team to lose all 10 of their opening matches of the season.
Hathilde Harviken’s late goal gave Aston Villa a 1-0 win over derby rivals Birmingham , which gives Brian Sørensen his third win since stepping in as interim manager and leaves his side seventh. Press Association
Slegers’s 50th WSL match in charge of the north London side almost ended in defeat late on but Alexia Putellas’s rising, stoppage-time strike flew narrowly over the bar. Regarding lying sixth in the table after 10 games, Slegers said “the season isn’t over, it’s still November”, before praising her team’s resurgence in their past three matches.
“The team is in a very good place,” she said. “The preparation, the dedication, the hunger for details, doing everything they possibly can – that’s the standard. Things are clicking well. But also the [opponents], they’re teams that spend time on the ball and that are brave and want to dominate games, so the types of games have been different.”
It certainly was different but the end result was the same for an Arsenal team still unable to find that elusive home win.

Arsenal Women vs London City Lionesses. Barclays Women's Super League.
Report and free match highlights as Arsenal's wait for a home WSL win goes on after a 1-1 draw against London City Lionesses; the Gunners have now drawn all five games at the Emirates this season; Frida Maanum's early strike was immediately cancelled out by Izzy Goodwin
Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player
Arsenal's wait for a home WSL win continues as they drew 1-1 against London City Lionesses on Sunday - their fifth draw in a row at the Emirates this season - with an inspired Mary Earps denying the Gunners victory.
While the result extends Arsenal's unbeaten home run to 24 league matches, it is becoming an increasing concern and a spectre on the shoulder that the Gunners have been unable to secure three points at the Emirates this year.
Giving her view to Sky Sports after the game, Renee Slegers - managing her 50th Arsenal game - said: "We spent more time than we normally do without the ball; partly the game plan and partly them asking questions of us on the pitch.
"We create big chances, could have done more with those. That's the frustrating part. This is the fifth [home game] and we couldn't give the fans the win. Unfortunately we couldn't do it for them."
It was two early goals that decided the fixture too. Frida Maanum scored for a second game in a row - having netted against Barcelona in the Champions League in midweek - slotting home from an Alessia Russo cross to put Arsenal ahead.
But a minute later, London City were level. Leah Williamson lost the run of the lively Izzy Goodwin, and the striker lashed into the roof of the net.
From then on, it was a goalkeeping masterclass from former England No 1 Earps especially that kept Arsenal from scoring another with her counterpart Misa Rodriguez also making her fair share of saves, albeit not as frequently.
The Gunners simply could not find a way past the inspired London City stopper as Lionesses boss Sarina Wiegman watched on from the stands.
The pick of her string of world-class saves came when she tipped a Maanum shot onto the crossbar. It came shortly after substitute Delphine Cascarino had also rattled the woodwork at the other end.
The result does little to improve either side's WSL standings, and Arsenal's hopes of finishing in the Champions League places takes another hit. They are sixth on 14 points - already six behind London City in third.
"We were happy with the one point, we wanted and needed three today," Slegers added. "Every game is three points for Arsenal when we play for this club.
"At the moment, with our position in the table and how we need to stay connected and compete for the top three positions for the Champions League, this one was very important for us.
"With that being said, the season isn't over. It's still November and we have to look at what it looks like in May."
10: GOAL! A sweeping move is finished by Maanum after Russo's cutback to give Arsenal the lead.
11: GOAL! London City immediately equalise as Goodwin fires into the roof of the net.
22: SAVE! Earps makes a good stop to deny Lisa Baum, who cuts in from the right-hand side.
27: SAVE! Misa Rodriguez on hand this time to deny Alexia Putellas.
29: SAVE! Again from Earps! This time it's a flying effort to keep out another Baum shot.
68: CROSSBAR! Cascarino pings an effort off the top of the woodwork.
77: DOUBLE SAVE! Earps pulls off another brilliant double save, first to deny Smith then Maanum.
85: CROSSBAR! Earps fingertips a Maanum shot onto the crossbar.
Before Sunday's game, S ky Sports asked whether Arsenal have lost their fear factor at the Emirates this season.
The answer surely has to be yes - although after the game, Slegers was adamant that the fear factor has not gone, despite being without a win.
Teams have come to the Emirates and sat in a low block that the Gunners have been unable to break down more than once.
London City were never going to do that. It's not in their DNA. They closer resemble the Barcelona team Arsenal faced on Thursday where, funnily enough, they drew 1-1.
But what they might not have been banking on was an ingenious performance from Earps. While Arsenal did not have to worry about defenders sitting back, they did face a goalkeeper putting in one of the performances of the season. How's your luck?
She made eight saves as Arsenal continued to pepper her goal - her most in the WSL since 2017 - and the second-most in the WSL this season after the goalkeeper that replaces her at Man Utd, Phallon Tullis-Joyce.
When asked how she found the game, Earps told Sky Sports: "Tiring. It's a big point away from home.
"Either team could have won it in terms of chances. Happy with the point - would have liked three. All the girls put their bodies on the line. I love defending. It was tough today and I thought we did a good job."
It was perhaps made all the sweeter for her that her former England boss Sarina Wiegman was watching on. It is well-documented how she departed the national team, but it certainly showed the Lionesses head coach what she was missing.
Earps has had to bide her time at London City, with Elene Lete continuing to be the No 1 until recently. The former England No 1 has now started in three games, and while she is yet to keep a clean sheet, she will have staked a huge claim to the permeant spot with her performance on Sunday.
"Mary is amazing," her boss Eder Maestre said after the game. "It's not just because of the talent she has, she delivers the commitment and the togetherness that she can bring to the team because of her experience. Watching her in that performance was a pleasure."
" Two good teams going against each other. I think we started the game well, score a very good goal, but we let them come back into the game too easily.
"I must say the players left everything on the pitch. They were absolutely dedicated, playing with hunger and focus. There are things in our game we must do better. We want to be dominating the ball. Being more ruthless. It's very basic but that's what it's about."
On Maanum: "She was very big for us against Barcelona and good for us tonight again. You can always count on her with runs into the box. The finish was very good."
On 50th Arsenal game: "I'm proud to represent Arsenal. I want to do everything I can for Arsenal."
"We are happy because this kind of environment is always difficult to cope with, but at the same time, we want to win every game so we cannot be [too happy] just because it's the first time we've drawn against Arsenal.
"Our targets are even bigger. We have the hop to have the performance. We improve quite well in the second half. We had the chances, and they did as well.
"They're one of the best teams in the world and playing knowing that they need the points to push for the Champions League positions. We already knew how close it was going to be."

Mario Frick has been announced as the new head coach of Aberdeen, taking over from the sacked Stephen Robinson to become the club's fourth manager in 2026.
Capped 125 times as a striker for Liechtenstein, the 52-year-old was last in charge at Luzern, leaving the Swiss club in the summer after five years.
He follows Robinson, Peter Leven and Jimmy Thelin in leading the side in this calendar year and will take charge for the first time against Scottish Premiership bottom side Kilmarnock on Saturday.
"Throughout our discussions, he demonstrated a clear vision, strong leadership qualities and a deep understanding of what is required to build a successful team," said Pittodrie chief executive Adrian Bevington.
"He was also exceptionally well regarded by the many people across the game we consulted during the process, and the board was unanimous in its belief that he is the right person to lead Aberdeen forward."
Former Motherwell and St Mirren boss Robinson was dismissed on 9 November, with Aberdeen second bottom of the table and having lost four games in a row in all competitions.
'Aberdeen hunt yet another manager after ill-fated Robinson reign'
Watch new Aberdeen boss Frick score against Scotland in September 2010
Frick, who also managed Vaduz in the Swiss Super League, will be assisted by Roman Matter and is the seventh permanent manager since Dave Cormack took control of the club in November 2019.
As a player, his former clubs include FC Basel, FC Zurich, St. Gallen and Grasshopper, while his 16 international goals make him Liechtenstein's all-time top scorer.
"Mario is a strong personality with clear ideas about how he wants his teams to play," added sporting director Lutz Pfannenstiel. "He brings energy, ambition and a winning mentality, and knows how to build a strong team environment.
"We were looking for the right person to lead the next chapter of Aberdeen FC, and I'm convinced Mario has the qualities, character and vision to make a real impact."
Frick got Vaduz promoted in 2020 before helping Luzern avoid relegation following his move there in 2021.
The next again year he guided them to a fourth-placed finish and European qualification, although they were knocked out of Conference League qualifying by Lee Johnson's Hibernian.
Aberdeen say Frick "has built a strong reputation for transforming teams, handing top-flight debuts to more than 30 academy players during his coaching career".
Hibs striker Thibault Klidje and current Aberdeen goalkeeper Marius Muller both played under him.
Aberdeen did not disclose contract details for Frick as he takes over a side with just three wins from 12 Premiership outings this season.
One of his international goals came at Hampden Park in 2010 when a late Stephen McManus header rescued a 2-1 win for Scotland.

Kev: Could be good. Could be bad. If it is the latter the the Dons will be in real trouble. It's a very quick appointment...
Sandra: Never heard of him but kudos to the club for acting in a timely manner for once. All the best Mario, you'll need it.
Malky: A curve ball if ever there was one. I admit I was unaware of him; I had to Google him. As far as I'm aware he has a 37% win ratio, so he'll fit right into the current state this club finds itself in. I hope to be proved wrong, but for me it's underwhelming.
Harry: He certainly can't be any worse than the last few that have come and gone. Surely gonna hit the jackpot at some point.

Gaziantep FK 'de başkan Memik Yılmaz , teknik direktör Volkan Demirel ile prensipte anlaştıklarını söyledi.
Yılmaz, bir otelde düzenlediği basın buluşmasında, takım olarak en çok kenetlenmeye ihtiyaç duydukları zaman diliminden geçtiklerini dile getirdi.
Takım için en iyi teknik direktörü bulmaya çalıştıklarını belirten Yılmaz, " Volkan Demirel ile prensipte anlaştık. Yarın takımın başında antrenmana çıkacak " ifadelerini kullandı.
Futbolculuk kariyerinin ardından Fenerbahçe'de antrenör olarak görev yapan Volkan Demirel, ilk teknik direktörlük deneyimini Aralık 2021'de Fatih Karagümrük'te yaşadı. Demirel, daha sonra Eylül 2022'de Hatayspor'un başına geçti ve Mayıs 2024'e kadar bu görevini sürdürdü.
2024-2025 sezonunda Bodrum FK'yi çalıştıran Demirel'in son durağı ise Gençlerbirliği oldu. Başkent ekibinde 2025-2026 sezonunda iki ayrı dönemde görev alan teknik direktörün son sözleşmesi Mayıs 2026'da sona erdi.

İngiliz müzisyen Phil Collins, cumartesi akşamı Los Angeles'taki Peacock Theater'da düzenlenen törenle Rock and Roll Hall of Fame'e solo sanatçı olarak kabul edildi. Collins, daha önce Genesis grubunun üyesi olarak da bu onura layık görülmüştü.
Collins'i sahneye Blink-182 grubunun davulcusu Travis Barker davet etti. Sağlık sorunları nedeniyle 2022'deki Genesis veda turnesinden bu yana sahneye çıkmayan 75 yaşındaki sanatçı, iki bastonla kürsüye yürüdü ve salondakiler tarafından ayakta alkışlandı.
Euronews'ün aktardığına göre Collins, mikrofonu aldığında "Göründüğüm kadar kötü değilim" dedi. Ünlü müzisyen, "Benden son duyduğunuz bu olmayacak, size söz verebilirim" diye ekledi.
Konuşması sırasında duygulanan Collins'i törende, oyuncu Lily Collins'in de aralarında bulunduğu çocukları izledi. Gecede Cynthia Erivo, sanatçının "In The Air Tonight" şarkısını seslendirirken Travis Barker da parçanın davul bölümünü çaldı.
Collins, tören sonrasında gazetecilere yaptığı açıklamada "Hayatım birbiri ardına gelen olaylardan, birbiri ardına gerçekleşen hayallerden ibaret oldu" dedi.
Aynı gece Wu-Tang Clan, Billy Idol, Queen Latifah, MC Lyte, Joy Division/New Order ve hayatını kaybeden Luther Vandross da Rock and Roll Hall of Fame'e kabul edildi. Bu yılın listesinde yer alan Oasis, Sade ve Iron Maiden ise törene katılmadı.

Izzy Goodwin scored from her one shot on target against Arsenal
After 10 games in the Women's Super League season, London City Lionesses have shown they are capable of finishing inside the top three.
Their narrow 2-1 defeat by Manchester City two weeks ago provided snippets of their potential but a 1-1 draw at the Emirates against an improved Arsenal on Sunday confirmed their credentials.
Eder Maestre's side sit third in the table - the last qualification spot for next season's Women's Champions League - and are six points above Arsenal.
It is a strong position to be in just shy of the halfway stage having already faced big hitters Arsenal, Manchester City and Manchester United.
Current leaders Chelsea await in December but, for now, London City's progress is moving at a pace that looks set to challenge the usual suspects.
Find interviews and extra content on the BBC Women's Football Weekly feed
Goodwin's glorious solo strike draws London City Lionesses level
A sold-out away end helped fill out the 32,000-strong crowd at the Emirates on Sunday as many hoped for an end-to-end encounter.
They were not disappointed as fearless London City showed bravery against an Arsenal side who played with a spark following their 1-1 draw with Barcelona.
The visitors were helped out by Arsenal's wastefulness - the Gunners had 17 shots and only converted one - but London City caused plenty of problems of their own.
Maestre said after their defeat by Manchester City that their opponents showed more experience and know-how but against Arsenal, his side matured.
They were under pressure early on and fell a goal down thanks to Frida Maanum's opener but it took just 98 seconds for Izzy Goodwin to equalise for London City.
That killed Arsenal's momentum and when the pressure increased again from the hosts in the second half, goalkeeper and player of the match Mary Earps stepped up to make crucial saves.
"The performance was there. We had the chances to score and get a better result but Arsenal had chances too. The game was very open," said Maestre.
"The way we faced and challenged every circumstance in the game shows we are here, and able to play with that mentality in these big games.
"We came here to take risks. Our energy was good. We were brave and weren't scared about the context or the opponent.
"We tried to play as if we were at home. I always want to feel that my teams are brave and go for the win."
That bravery showed as Alexia Putellas came close twice with long-range efforts, Goodwin could have been onside when she was played in behind later on.
London City hit the crossbar through substitute Delphine Cascarino and had 14 shots compared to Arsenal's 17, including four inside the box.
Arsenal are still yet to win at home this season in the WSL but this was still an impressive showing from London City, who came to the Emirates to play.
But while they were willing to take risks, they were smarter than they were against Manchester City, choosing when to press aggressively and when to hold off.
"We tried to match the pace of the ball and not expose ourselves as much to the players that Arsenal have," added Maestre.
"We were trying to mix the moments we were more clinical in our press. We made some adjustments at half-time and were much better at recognising those."
London City are backed by US billionaire Michele Kang and that has made a big difference in the transfer market.
They recruited superstars Alexia Putellas, Mary Earps, Mapi Leon and Kadidiatou Diani in the summer.
Such is their depth that high-flying Spaniard Lucia Corrales, the dangerous Cascarino and England international Freya Godfrey came off the bench.
Those individual talents have made a difference and on Sunday it was goalkeeper Earps who took the plaudits, claiming the player of the match award.
She made crucial saves late on as Arsenal pushed ferociously for a winner, tipping Maanum's effort onto the crossbar and blocking her shot from close range.
Earps had to bide her time for the number one shirt after making the switch from Paris St-Germain this summer but has started the past three WSL games.
"Mary is a very strong character and is much more than the things we see in terms of the performance," said Maestre.
"She has experience, and energy that you can bring to every part in the process and not just the things we see in the matches.
"I think the energy that she brings to the position is massive and has a massive impact. I'm very pleased with her."
Watching on in the stands was England boss Sarina Wiegman who will have been pleased with the display from goalscorer Goodwin.
The 23-year-old got the better of England captain Leah Williamson when she fooled her with quick feet and fired the ball into the back of the net, making it 1-1.
She is proof that competition for places in the London City starting XI is pushing players on and that their depth is improving each week.
"I think Izzy is becoming a more mature player. She has the inner competition and the signings sometimes push you to bring 100% every time," added Maestre.
"She is committed to keep pushing and, with the performances she is having, why not [earn an England call-up]?
"Izzy is moving forward in the ways she can take advantage and that commitment is the way she is reaching those performances. I'm very proud of her."

texts.https://www.hurriyet.com.tr/sporarena/fr:
UEFA Uluslar A Ligi 1. Grup’taki son mücadelesinde A Milli Futbol Takımımımız, Fransa’ya konuk oluyor. İlk beş karşılaşmasını kaybederek puansız şekilde son sırada kalan ay-yıldızlılar, Fransa deplasmanında ilk galibiyetini arayacak.
Türkiye ile Fransa, UEFA Uluslar A Ligi 1. Grup altıncı maçında yarın oynayacakları maçla 8. kez karşılaşacak. Geride kalan 7 maçta Türkiye 1, Fransa 5 kez galip geldi, 1 maç da beraberlikle sona erdi. Dördü resmi, üçü özel olmak üzere geride kalan 7 maçta Fransa 14, Türkiye ise 5 gol attı.
Müsabaka öncesi karşılıklı olarak açıklamalar gelmeye devam ediyor. Bunlardan biri de Fransa Teknik Direktörü Zinedine Zidane’dan geldi. Telefoot yayınına konuk olan Fransız teknik adam İtalya karşısında aldıkları mağlubiyetten ders çıkardığını ve paniklemediğini söyledi.
Mbappe’nin ilk 11’de maça başlayacağını söyleyen Zidane "Mbappé mi? Evet, ilk 11'de başlayacak. Her halükarda, kaptanımız Kylian'ın geri dönmesinden mutluyum. Ve yarın da geri dönmesinden mutluyum. Normal şekilde antrenman yapacak, yani her şey yolunda." İfadelerini kullandı.
Sonrasında Türkiye’nin eksiklerinin olmasının kendilerini rahatlatmadığının altını çizen Fransız adam Milli Takımımız ve Arda Güler hakkında şöyle konuştu:
"Türkiye'de bazı oyuncular eksik olduğunda işlerin zorlaşabileceği düşünülebilir, bu doğru. Ancak Arda Güler , her zaman takımına etki etmeyi başarıyor. Bu da nasıl bir oyuncu olduğunu kanıtlıyor."

Kıbrıs’ta hayranlarıyla buluşan İrem Derici, evlilik planlarına ilişkin soruyu esprili bir dille yanıtladı. Derici, yaz boyunca kazandıklarını evine harcadığını anlattı.
Konser öncesinde gazetecilerin sorularını yanıtlayan Derici’ye, nişanlısı DJ Melih Kunukçu ile evlilik planları soruldu. Ev tadilatı nedeniyle bütçelerinin tükendiğini söyleyen Derici, “Paramız kalmadı!” yanıtını verdi.
Yaz boyunca kazandıklarını evine harcadığını anlatan Derici, “Ben bütün yaz eve çalıştım. Kasa boş, kasa bomboş! Banka hesabım gitgide düşüyor” ifadelerini kullandı.
Gündemdeki yapay zekâ tartışmasına ilişkin görüşünü de paylaşan Derici, “Yapay zekâ bize yeni bir şey vermiyor. Elimizde olanları hızlıca hizmet olarak veriyor” diye konuştu.
Derici, Paris Moda Haftası’nda podyuma çıkan oyuncu Serenay Sarıkaya’ya da övgüler yağdırdı. Derici, “Oyunculuğuna zaten bayılıyordum. Ama oradaki duruşu, kendine güveni çok başka bir şey... Hayran kaldım” dedi.
